hunks.baseline: “The important fact is that the duel was fair!”
hunks.sol: “The important thing is that the duel was fair!”

hunks.baseline: “Fair? Since when is using poison considered fair? Is this the Sichuan Tang Clan or something?”
hunks.sol: “Fair? Since when is using poison considered fair? What is this, the Sichuan Tang Clan?”

hunks.baseline: “Of course the Third Young Master would say he didn’t. And how can you believe that quack?”
hunks.sol: “Of course the Third Young Master would deny it. And how can you trust that quack?”

hunks.baseline: “A quack? You little bastard!”
hunks.sol: “A quack? You bastard!”

hunks.baseline: “If necessary, we should stop the war even if it means offering up the Third Young Master’s head!”
hunks.sol: “If necessary, we should prevent the war even if it means offering up the Third Young Master’s head!”

hunks.baseline: “What kind of outrageous nonsense is that?”
hunks.sol: “What outrageous nonsense!”

hunks.baseline: “Am I wrong? Let’s just admit it. The Mount Heng Sword Sect is stronger than our family. If war begins, hundreds will die or be injured, and in the worst case, our family could be destroyed. If we hand over the Third Young Master, who caused all this, won’t everything be over?”
hunks.sol: “Am I wrong? Let’s admit it already. The Mount Heng Sword Sect is stronger than our family. If war breaks out, hundreds will be killed or injured, and in the worst case, our family will be wiped out. If we hand over the Third Young Master, who caused all this, won’t that settle everything?”

hunks.baseline: What kind of bullshit was that? I hadn’t heard such spectacular nonsense in a long time. The back of my neck tightened, and my chest grew tight.
hunks.sol: Was that supposed to be speech or a fart? It had been a while since I’d heard bullshit that impressive. The back of my neck tightened, and my chest began to ache.

hunks.baseline: His voice was quiet, but it carried power. In fact, its quietness made it sound even clearer.
hunks.sol: His voice was quiet, but it carried power. Its very quietness made it all the clearer.

hunks.baseline: It was Jin Wikyung. He looked around the room with an expressionless face.
hunks.sol: It was Jin Wikyung. He looked around the room, his face expressionless.

hunks.baseline: “Whose. Head. Did you say we’d offer?”
hunks.sol: “Whose. Head. Did you say we should offer?”

hunks.baseline: Each syllable fell separately, frost coating his voice. The atmosphere was so chilling that even I shivered.
hunks.sol: Frost coated every clipped syllable. The atmosphere was so chilling that even I shivered, but the White Tiger Hall Master immediately spoke up.

hunks.baseline: The White Tiger Hall Leader spoke up at once.
“Obviously, the Third Young Master, the main culprit behind this—ah.”
hunks.sol: “Why, obviously the Third Young Master, the chief culprit behind this—ah.”

hunks.baseline: That bastard was bald, and he couldn’t read the room either. The White Tiger Hall Leader let his words trail off, but it was already too late.
hunks.sol: That bastard had no hair and no sense of danger, either. The White Tiger Hall Master trailed off, but it was already too late.

hunks.baseline: “So you intend to hand the Third Young Master’s head over to the Mount Heng Sword Sect over something that has not even been confirmed? Is that something a hall leader of this family should be saying?”
hunks.sol: “So you intend to offer the Third Young Master’s head to the Mount Heng Sword Sect over something that hasn’t even been confirmed? Is that something a hall master of this family should say?”

hunks.baseline: “No, that’s not what I meant…”
hunks.sol: “No, that isn’t what I meant…”

hunks.baseline: The White Tiger Hall Leader was overwhelmed by Jin Wikyung’s aura and avoided his eyes. Jin Wikyung silently glared at him.
hunks.sol: Overwhelmed by Jin Wikyung’s aura, the White Tiger Hall Master avoided his gaze. Jin Wikyung stared silently at him.

hunks.baseline: He wasn’t normally like this, which made him even scarier now that he was angry.
hunks.sol: He was usually so mild that seeing him angry made him even more frightening.

hunks.baseline: Looking at the White Tiger Hall Leader’s pale face made me feel as if ten years of indigestion had finally been cured. Jin Wikyung rose from his seat and looked down at everyone with a cold expression.
hunks.sol: The White Tiger Hall Master’s deathly pale face made me feel as though ten years of indigestion had finally cleared. Jin Wikyung rose from his seat and looked coldly over the gathering.

hunks.baseline: “You all already know.”
hunks.sol: “You all know the truth already.”

hunks.baseline: He looked around the room and spoke firmly.
hunks.sol: He swept his gaze across the room and spoke with conviction.

hunks.baseline: “That the duel was fair, and Lee Seogeun’s poisoning was a conspiracy. Knowing that, are you suggesting we submit to them out of fear?”
hunks.sol: “The duel was fair, and Lee Seogeun’s poisoning was a conspiracy. Knowing that, are you suggesting we surrender to them out of fear?”

hunks.baseline: The members of the Elder Council faction avoided his gaze. Jin Wikyung’s sneer grew deeper.
hunks.sol: The members of the Council of Elders faction avoided his gaze. Jin Wikyung’s sneer deepened.

hunks.baseline: “I don’t know who placed it in their hands, but the Mount Heng Sword Sect holds the hilt of a sword called justification. Whether it happens today or tomorrow—or whether the sword has already been drawn—we are already too late to reverse it. There is only one way forward. We fight.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know who placed it in their hands, but the Mount Heng Sword Sect now holds the hilt of a sword called justification. Whether they strike today or tomorrow—or whether the sword has already been drawn—it’s too late for us to turn this around. There is only one thing we can do. Fight back.”

hunks.baseline: “Do you want to live? Do you want to protect the family? If you truly do, prepare the martial artists and prepare for war. Or cut off my head and my younger brother’s, then offer them to the Mount Heng Sword Sect. If all you want is wealth and glory, I suppose that isn’t a bad option, either.”
hunks.sol: “Do you want to live? Do you want to protect the family? If you truly do, ready the martial artists and prepare for war. Otherwise, cut off my head and my younger brother’s and offer them up. If wealth and glory are all you desire, I suppose that isn’t a bad option.”

hunks.baseline: A suffocating silence took over the main assembly hall.
hunks.sol: A suffocating silence seized the main assembly hall.

hunks.baseline: If one person hadn’t opened his mouth the next moment, we might have been crushed beneath that silence for hours.
hunks.sol: If one person hadn’t spoken the next moment, we might have remained crushed beneath that silence for hours.

hunks.baseline: It was the man who had watched the situation without saying a word until now.
hunks.sol: It was the man who had silently watched everything unfold until now.

hunks.baseline: A person to watch out for. The family’s highest-ranking elder and the head of the Council of Elders.
hunks.sol: Someone I needed to watch. The family’s highest-ranking elder and the head of the Council of Elders.

hunks.baseline: I remembered the Sound Transmission Jin Wikyung had sent me earlier.
hunks.sol: I recalled Jin Wikyung’s earlier Sound Transmission.

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung was the greatest ally and adviser I had among the NPCs.
hunks.sol: Among all the NPCs, Jin Wikyung was my greatest ally and adviser.

hunks.baseline: If someone asked me to count the number of NPCs I had encountered even once since starting this godforsaken game, the number would easily be over a hundred.
hunks.sol: If someone asked me to count every NPC I’d encountered since starting this godforsaken game, the number would easily exceed a hundred.

hunks.baseline: Each of them had their own expressions and personalities. The servant I met at the pleasure house wore a business smile worn down by life. The coachman who brought me here had a goofy side. The senior members I met in the family were surprisingly simple-minded and aggressive.
hunks.sol: They each had their own expressions and personalities. The servant I met at the pleasure house wore the weary professional smile of someone ground down by life. The coachman who brought me here had a bumbling side, while the senior members of the family were surprisingly simple and hot-tempered.

hunks.sol: *I can’t read him.*

hunks.baseline: When the interrogation began. When the senior members of each faction shouted at one another. And even now.
hunks.sol: When the interrogation began. When the senior members of the different factions shouted at one another. Even now.

hunks.baseline: “I thought of you as nothing more than a youngster, but before I knew it, the Lesser Family Head had become such a dignified martial artist. Excellent. That is how the Lesser Family Head of our family should be.”
hunks.sol: “I had always thought of you as a mere youngster, but before I knew it, the Lesser Family Head had grown into such a commanding martial artist. Excellent. That is how the Lesser Family Head of our family should conduct himself.”

hunks.baseline: “I can only apologize for showing you such an unseemly side.”
hunks.sol: “I can only apologize for showing you such an unseemly sight.”

hunks.baseline: “Excessive humility can look like arrogance. You have nothing to apologize for.”
hunks.sol: “Excessive humility can be mistaken for arrogance. You have nothing to apologize for.”

hunks.baseline: Despite the Head Elder’s praise, Jin Wikyung’s face remained stiff.
hunks.sol: Despite the Head Elder’s praise, Jin Wikyung’s expression remained stiff.

hunks.baseline: “May this old man add a word? What do you think, Lesser Family Head?”
hunks.sol: “May this old man add a few words? What do you think, Lesser Family Head?”

hunks.baseline: “I will take it to heart.”
hunks.sol: “I will take them to heart.”

hunks.baseline: The Head Elder slowly rose from his seat, and dozens of pairs of eyes locked onto him.
hunks.sol: As the Head Elder slowly rose, dozens of pairs of eyes fixed on him.

hunks.baseline: He was the family’s highest-ranking elder. In terms of authority and standing within the family, he might even surpass Jin Wikyung.
hunks.sol: He was the family’s most senior elder. In authority and standing within the family, he might even surpass Jin Wikyung.

hunks.baseline: The biggest problem was that he was the head of the opposing faction—the Elder Council.
hunks.sol: The biggest problem was that he led the opposing faction, the Council of Elders.

hunks.baseline: *Fuck, I’m screwed.*
hunks.sol: *Fuck. I’m screwed.*

hunks.baseline: Preparing for the worst, I started edging toward the door when the Head Elder’s first words reached my ears.
hunks.sol: I began inching toward the door in preparation for the worst when the Head Elder’s first words reached my ears.

hunks.baseline: I whipped my head around. The Head Elder still wore that same strange smile.
hunks.sol: I whipped my head around. The Head Elder still wore his usual strange smile.

hunks.baseline: “Even beasts join forces and fight when an enemy enters their den. And yet men who are supposedly senior members of this family offer up the head of a direct-line member as a solution to stop a war. Heh. So men like this sit in our family council.”
hunks.sol: “Even beasts join forces to fight when an enemy enters their den. Yet men who call themselves senior members of this family propose offering up the head of a direct descendant to prevent a war. Heh. To think men like you sit on our family council.”

hunks.baseline: “N-no, Head Elder. You’ve misunderstood. It was merely…”
hunks.sol: “N-no, Head Elder. You misunderstand. It was merely…”

hunks.baseline: “White Tiger Hall Leader.”
hunks.sol: “White Tiger Hall Master.”

hunks.baseline: At the Head Elder’s chilly call, the White Tiger Hall Leader stiffened.
hunks.sol: At the Head Elder’s icy call, the White Tiger Hall Master stiffened.

hunks.baseline: “Have I been away for too long? Or is it because the Family Head is absent?”
hunks.sol: “Was I away for too long? Or is this what happened because the Family Head was absent?”

hunks.baseline: Going by the Head Elder’s expression, he looked like a muscular old man at a gym asking whether you’d eaten. But the content of his words was vicious beyond belief.
hunks.sol: Judging by his expression alone, he looked like some ripped old man at the gym asking if you’d eaten. But his words were downright vicious.

hunks.baseline: *What is this?*
hunks.sol: *What the hell is this?*

hunks.baseline: I looked around frantically, but everyone else was just as confused as I was. Both factions were visibly flustered.
hunks.sol: I darted my eyes around, but everyone else looked just as confused as I was. Both factions were visibly flustered.

hunks.baseline: “If war has become inevitable, then our first priority should be to discipline those within our ranks. Wouldn’t it be best to cut off the heads of those men who are little different from rebels?”
hunks.sol: “If war is now inevitable, our first priority should be putting our own house in order. Shouldn’t we begin by cutting off the heads of those men who are little better than traitors?”

hunks.baseline: In the frozen air, Jin Wikyung stared at the Head Elder for a long moment before answering in something like a sigh.
hunks.sol: In the frozen silence, Jin Wikyung stared at the Head Elder for a long moment before letting out his answer like a sigh.

hunks.baseline: Whew. The White Tiger Hall Leader let out a relieved sigh.
hunks.sol: Whew. The White Tiger Hall Master breathed a sigh of relief.

hunks.baseline: Considering how he had just been talking about offering up my head, I was a little disappointed.
hunks.sol: Considering that he’d just suggested offering up my head, I was a little disappointed.

hunks.baseline: *Should I suggest that we kill just him?*
hunks.sol: *Should I suggest killing just him?*

hunks.baseline: “Those men not only framed a direct-line member of the family, but even argued we should hand him over to the enemy. Don’t you think that is too lenient a response?”
hunks.sol: “Those men not only slandered a direct descendant of the family but argued that we should hand him over to the enemy. Don’t you think you’re being too lenient?”

hunks.baseline: “They have served our family loyally for many years. I will consider it an ill-considered remark made in the heat of the moment.”
hunks.sol: “They have served our family faithfully for many years. I will consider their words a thoughtless remark made in the heat of the moment.”

hunks.baseline: “An ill-considered remark. An ill-considered remark, indeed. Yes. The Lesser Family Head’s capacity is greater than I expected. Truly worthy of being the Lesser Family Head. In that case, I will not hold them responsible. I offer my thanks to the Lesser Family Head for magnanimously forgiving the thoughtless words of old men.”
hunks.sol: “A thoughtless remark. A thoughtless remark, indeed. Yes, the Lesser Family Head’s capacity is greater than I imagined. You are truly worthy of your position. In that case, I will not hold them accountable. I offer my thanks to the Lesser Family Head for magnanimously forgiving the thoughtless words of these old men.”

hunks.baseline: When the Head Elder bowed, the others hurriedly waved their hands and bent at the waist in return.
hunks.sol: When the Head Elder bowed, the others frantically waved their hands and bent at the waist in return.

hunks.baseline: “Oh, Head Elder, no. Our thoughts were shallow.”
hunks.sol: “Oh, Head Elder, please. We were the ones who failed to think matters through.”

hunks.baseline: “Please, don’t do this.”
hunks.sol: “Please don’t do this.”

hunks.baseline: “Head Elder!”
hunks.sol: “Head Elder…!”

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung was the one who had spared them, yet they were making a huge scene.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung was the one who had spared them, yet they were making a huge fuss over the Head Elder.

hunks.baseline: Go on, put on a show. A real show.
hunks.sol: Go on. Put on a show. What a performance.

hunks.baseline: I was watching the spectacle with a private click of my tongue when—
hunks.sol: I clicked my tongue inwardly as I watched the spectacle.

hunks.baseline: An indescribable sense of wrongness settled over me. I hurriedly examined the people gathered around the Head Elder.
hunks.sol: An indescribable sense of wrongness swept over me. I hurriedly examined the people gathered around the Head Elder.

hunks.baseline: And then I noticed it.
hunks.sol: And then I saw it.

hunks.baseline: The smiles flickering around the lips of the Elder Council members who had pressured me earlier.
hunks.sol: The faint smiles flickering across the lips of the Council of Elders members who had hounded me earlier.

hunks.baseline: Was this all planned? Every bit of it?
hunks.sol: Was this planned? All of it?

hunks.baseline: Why? For what purpose? Countless questions rose and vanished. My thoughts were a complete mess.
hunks.sol: What were they trying to accomplish? Why? Countless questions rose and vanished. My thoughts were a complete mess.

hunks.baseline: I didn’t even need to turn around to look for him. The Head Elder was already holding Jin Wikyung’s hand high in the air and shouting.
hunks.sol: I didn’t even need to turn and look for him. The Head Elder was already raising Jin Wikyung’s hand high in the air and shouting.

hunks.baseline: “With the Family Head absent, the Lesser Family Head is effectively the Family Head. I support the Lesser Family Head in this matter. If we unite around him, then no matter how formidable they are, they will not dare challenge the Jin Family!”
hunks.sol: “With the Family Head absent, the Lesser Family Head is effectively our Family Head. I support him in this matter. If we unite behind him, then no matter how formidable our enemies may be, they will never dare challenge the Jin Family!”

hunks.baseline: The heated atmosphere. The people’s cheers and shouts.
hunks.sol: The heated atmosphere. The chanting and cheers.

hunks.baseline: It felt strangely familiar.
hunks.sol: It all felt strangely familiar.

hunks.baseline: The moment I saw the corners of Jin Wikyung’s mouth quiver and the Head Elder’s strange smile, I realized where that familiar feeling came from.
hunks.sol: The moment I saw the corners of Jin Wikyung’s mouth tremble and the Head Elder’s strange smile, I realized what it reminded me of.

hunks.baseline: The Head Elder’s figure overlapped with the politicians I had seen on television.
hunks.sol: The Head Elder’s figure overlapped with the politicians I’d seen on television.

hunks.baseline: It was deeply unsettling, but once the Head Elder raised Jin Wikyung’s hand, the meeting proceeded swiftly.
hunks.sol: The whole thing left a bad taste in my mouth, but once the Head Elder raised Jin Wikyung’s hand, the meeting proceeded at a rapid pace.

hunks.baseline: The discussion about the duel, which the Elder Council faction had stubbornly kept dragging out, disappeared entirely. Instead, the meeting focused on preparing for war.
hunks.sol: All discussion of the duel, which the Council of Elders faction had so stubbornly dragged out, vanished. Instead, the meeting focused on the assumption that war was coming.

hunks.baseline: “If we call back the martial artists stationed outside, roughly two hundred.”
hunks.sol: “If we recall the martial artists stationed outside… roughly two hundred.”

hunks.baseline: As many as two hundred?
hunks.sol: Two hundred?

hunks.baseline: I was astonished by the unexpectedly large number, but the next question made me shut my mouth.
hunks.sol: I was impressed by the unexpectedly large number, but the next question shut me up.

hunks.baseline: “If we select only elites of First Rate or higher?”
hunks.sol: “And if we select only elites of First Rate or higher?”

hunks.baseline: “Fewer than twenty. Of course, that number would be different if we included everyone present.”
hunks.sol: “Fewer than twenty. Of course, the number would be different if we included everyone present.”

hunks.baseline: I didn’t know much about the circumstances here, but that seemed like a decent number.
hunks.sol: I didn’t know much about how things worked here, but that seemed like a respectable number.

hunks.baseline: As expected of a prestigious family with deep roots. Two hundred years of accumulated strength didn’t simply vanish.
hunks.sol: Just what I’d expect from an old, prestigious great family. Two hundred years of accumulated strength didn’t simply vanish.

hunks.baseline: Three hundred. And that was the minimum, meaning there was a difference of more than a hundred men.
hunks.sol: Three hundred. And that was the minimum, which put them more than a hundred men ahead.

hunks.baseline: But it was fine. Fights came down to numbers anyway—
hunks.sol: But that was fine. Fights weren’t decided by numbers alone—

hunks.baseline: This war was going to be difficult.
hunks.sol: This war was going to be tough.

hunks.baseline: Still, with masters like Jin Wikyung and Wipeng, it was a fight worth attempting. They were high-level NPCs beyond what my Qi Sense could read. The Head Elder probably belonged to that category, too.
hunks.sol: Still, with masters like Jin Wikyung and Wipeng, we had a chance. They were high-level NPCs beyond the reach of my Qi Sense. The Head Elder probably belonged in the same category.

hunks.baseline: …This was so damn hopeless I couldn’t even deal with it.
hunks.sol: …Fuck this. I couldn’t do it.

hunks.baseline: *What? A prestigious family with deep roots? Two hundred years of history?*
hunks.sol: *What? An old, prestigious great family? Two hundred years of history?*

hunks.baseline: What the hell had these bastards been doing for two hundred years? I heard the Mount Heng Sword Sect had existed for less than thirty, but in terms of military strength, we weren’t merely outmatched.
hunks.sol: What the hell had these bastards been doing for two hundred years? From what I’d heard, the Mount Heng Sword Sect hadn’t even existed for thirty, yet their forces didn’t merely outmatch ours.

hunks.baseline: We were being steamrolled. Steamrolled.
hunks.sol: They crushed us. Completely.

hunks.baseline: *Did the Black Death sweep through last year or something?*
hunks.sol: *Did the Black Death sweep through here last year or something?*

hunks.baseline: Whether there had been a plague or not, I felt like I was going insane. I was staring at the meeting-hall ceiling, which had yellowed before I knew it, when I suddenly made a decision.
hunks.sol: Plague or no plague, I felt like I was about to lose my mind. As I stared at the yellowed ceiling of the meeting hall, I made a sudden decision.

hunks.sol: “From this moment onward, our family enters a state of war. Without my seal, no one may enter or leave the family grounds, regardless of rank or position. Maintain the strictest vigilance. Do not let so much as a single ant through. Understood?”
